passage: In the Class 6 art room in Kolkata, Nazia took the marker out of Bidisha's hand. "Not there. The title goes at the top, in blue." She rearranged every picture Ravi had pasted. Bidisha stepped back and folded her arms. Ravi went to sharpen a pencil that did not need sharpening. Nazia's poster looked neat, but the room had gone quiet. She noticed the dragging feet and the glance between the other two. "Do you have an idea?" she asked, slower. Bidisha said, "I wanted the river drawn in a curve." "Fine, you do the river. Ravi does the labels." It was not perfect; the curve wobbled. But everyone was talking again.

qa.q: What colour did Nazia say the title should be?
What might Bidisha have been feeling when she stepped back and folded her arms?
qa.a: Shut out and maybe annoyed, since her marker was taken and she had an idea for the river that nobody had asked about.

qa.q: What could Nazia keep doing to make the project feel shared?
qa.a: Ask for ideas, give each person a part, and accept that the result may be a bit wobbly.

qa.q: How might Ravi see the situation?
qa.a: Ravi went to sharpen a pencil that did not need sharpening, so Ravi probably felt uncomfortable and unneeded while Nazia took over.

grounding: A child takes over the project because she thinks only her way is right, then notices others feel shut out, listens, and gives each person a part.

passage:
The model for the science fair was due tomorrow, and the school hall was packed and noisy. Jyoti grabbed the glue gun from Naveen. "No, not like that. I'll do it."
She'd already redone Naveen's labels and moved Priti's cardboard hills. They stood back, arms folded.
"Jyoti, we can't do anything if you do everything," Naveen said.
Jyoti stopped. She looked at their faces. They looked shut out.
"Sorry. I just want it to be perfect."
"It doesn't have to be perfect. It has to be ours."
Jyoti took a breath. "Naveen, you glue the base. Priti, the hills. I'll do the labels." The model had a crooked tree. It was fine.

qa.q: What did Jyoti grab from Naveen?
How did Jyoti feel when Naveen spoke up?
qa.a: She felt caught and a bit embarrassed, seeing that her group felt shut out.

qa.q: What did Jyoti do that helped the group?
qa.a: She apologised, gave each person a part and accepted a crooked tree.

qa.q: How might Naveen feel about Jyoti taking over?
qa.a: Naveen felt shut out and frustrated, standing with arms folded.

grounding: A girl takes over the project because she thinks only her way is right; seeing others shut out, she gives everyone a part and accepts imperfection.

passage:
Thomas took over the poster in the Chennai school art room. He rubbed out Disha's lettering and redrew it. He moved all of Kiran's pictures.
Disha sat back and said nothing. Kiran stared out of the window.
Mrs Pillai walked by. "Thomas, is everyone working?"
Thomas looked round. Disha and Kiran weren't doing anything. Because of him.
"I think I've been bossy," he said quietly.
Disha shrugged. "A bit."
"Sorry. Disha, you do the lettering your way. Kiran, you choose where the pictures go. I'll colour the border."
The poster wasn't exactly how Thomas pictured it. But everyone had done a part.

qa.q: What did Thomas do to Disha's lettering?
qa.a: He rubbed it out and redrew it.

qa.q: How did Thomas feel when he looked round at Disha and Kiran?
qa.a: He felt uncomfortable and a bit ashamed, realising he had shut them out.

qa.q: How did Thomas change his approach?
qa.a: He gave each person a part and accepted the poster not being exactly how he pictured it.

qa.q: How might Disha have felt when Thomas rubbed out her work?
qa.a: Disha felt dismissed and shut out, sitting back and saying nothing.

grounding: A boy takes over a group poster, thinking only his way is right; noticing others shut out, he gives each a part and accepts imperfection.
